bullets.title: Fed's Waller opens door to hold in Sept; markets rally on dovish tilt
bullets.body: Governor Waller signaled he favors a rate hold in September unless CPI/PPI data come in hot — even a 0.30% core PCE print would be dovish enough to hold. Markets responded sharply: 2Y yields -6bp, 10Y -4bp, gold +2.86%, equities higher. The September FOMC decision is viewed as roughly 50/50, with Warsh seen as more hawkish and Williams more symmetrical on data.

bullets.title: August ISM Services beat at 55.4 but prices paid hit 4-year high — sticky inflation signal
bullets.body: ISM Services rose +1.3ppt to 55.4 in August, well above the +0.1ppt consensus expectation, with new orders at highest since January 2022 and backlogs surging. However, prices paid jumped +2.3ppt to a 4-year high, diverging from manufacturing, reflecting stickiness in PCE supercore services. Employment remained in contraction territory despite the overall activity beat.

bullets.title: Hedgeye raises inflation nowcast to +3.55% y/y; oil and Middle East risk keeping yields elevated
bullets.body: Hedgeye's September inflation nowcast shifted to a modest inflationary bias at +3.55% y/y, with August CPI expected at +3.50% y/y (+14bp sequential acceleration). Middle East energy disruption is the primary volatility driver; oil is signaling higher highs/lows, keeping the inflation nowcast ticking up and supporting the view that bond yields remain rangebound at 4.68–4.84% on the 10Y.

bullets.title: Initial claims 206k, labor market steady; vol-control flows set to inject ~$17B into SPX
bullets.body: Initial claims rose 2k w/w to 206k with the 13-week average down 8.6% y/y — consistent with a steady but slow re-hiring environment. Separately, one-month realized vol collapsing below three-month realized vol is expected to trigger ~$17B of net SPX buying from vol-control strategies as the June 5 -2.6% return rolls out of three-month realized vol.

bullets.title: S&P 500 consolidating, market narrowing not broadening; tech in largest 60-day drawdown ever
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes the S&P 500 is consolidating in a tight range (lower high, higher low) with VIX back in investable territory; they sold broad positions (RSP, VOX) and are buying selectively in Software and Healthcare. Jefferies flags tech turned negative YTD after a +128% rally through June 22, now in its largest 60-day drawdown ever, while Tech and Healthcare have become inversely correlated since late June.

bullets.title: SNOW blowout drives infrastructure software flows; sector rotation into software accelerating
bullets.body: Snowflake's +20% quarter with a path to +40% growth in 2H and a +22% stock move on the day is pulling the strongest net buying into Infrastructure Software since MSFT earnings, per Jefferies flow data. Internet is the second-best buy in tech on flows; Application Software seeing continued hedge fund buying. IGV +3.6% YTD vs S&P 500 +13.4% YTD, but SaaS multiples expanded 4–5% week-over-week.

bullets.title: AI frontier model price war accelerating: Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta all cut prices and expand agentic capability
bullets.body: Anthropic cut Fable 5.1 cache-read pricing 75% to $0.25/M tokens; OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol 20-33%; Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 offers near-parity intelligence (62 vs 63 on index) at materially lower cost with 25% fewer tokens. The pattern of lower per-token pricing paired with expanded agentic capability is empirically driving volume growth — agentic workloads consume 15-100x the compute of human-prompted usage.

bullets.title: AVGO FY28 AI revenue framework $230B — well above buy-side $200B; stock a patience trade
bullets.body: Broadcom's AI semi revenues hit $16.7B in the quarter (+221% YoY) with XPU shipments >3.5x YoY; FY27 AI revenue guided to ~$115B (doubling) and FY28 to $230B (doubling again) with $30 EPS. Four >10% AI customers expected in FY28 (GOOGL, META, two frontier labs). The stock -3% on the day as the near-term setup is less compelling than the FY28 story; a multi-year take-or-pay LTA with Google provides a floor.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI recovery is the pivotal variable for S&P 500 fair value; downside risk is -26% if cash returns don't normalize
bullets.body: 22V calculates S&P 500 fair value at ~$7,740 (roughly current levels) assuming cash returns recover from a record-low 56% to 80% over five years. If cash returns remain depressed, fair value falls to ~$5,660, implying -26% downside. The implied ERP of 4.7% (66th percentile) could compress to 4.0–4.25% if confidence builds in AI capex ROI.

bullets.title: Semiconductor tariff expansion risk: Section 232 tariffs may broaden to servers and PCs after Sept 24 Trump-Xi meeting
bullets.body: The Trump administration is reportedly considering expanding Section 232 semiconductor tariffs beyond the existing 25% to cover servers, PCs, and other electronics. A Phase 2 announcement could follow the Trump-Xi meeting on September 24, with enactment likely January 2027, creating a meaningful overhang for the hardware supply chain heading into year-end.

bullets.title: MSFT segment re-segmentation improves Azure transparency; makes it directly comparable to hyperscaler peers
bullets.body: Microsoft restructured into two segments — Agents & Infrastructure and Devices & Consumer — making Azure a cleaner consumption KPI with quarterly disclosure. Multiple sell-side desks view this as improving comparability vs. AWS and GCP and as a positive signal on Azure's confidence in growth trajectory.

bullets.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor suffer simultaneous outages starting ~9AM ET
bullets.body: OpenAI, Claude/Anthropic, Grok, and Cursor users all reported elevated error rates beginning around 9AM ET on September 3, with outages confirmed on company status pages and continuing through midday. Google Gemini also saw an uptick in error reports. The simultaneous nature raises questions about shared infrastructure dependencies across frontier AI providers.

bullets.title: Big Tech regulatory pressure mounts: AAPL $2.7B UK suit, AMZN FTC suit, GOOGL ad-tech breakup denied
bullets.body: Apple faces a $2.7B UK lawsuit over allegedly discriminatory app tracking rules; Amazon was sued by the FTC and 22 US states for raising advertiser prices without disclosure; a federal judge denied the DoJ's bid to break up Google's ad tech business, opting for behavioral remedies instead. RDDT and RBLX were designated as Very Large Online Platforms under EU DSA, subjecting them to the strictest regulatory scrutiny.

bullets.title: iPhone 18 launches Sept 9 with foldable Ultra at $2,000+; TSMC sole A20 beneficiary, Luxshare gains share
bullets.body: Citi forecasts 61.8M iPhone 18 shipments in 2H26, including 7.5M foldable units. The iPhone Ultra starts at $2,000+ and Pro/Pro Max are ~$200 higher than prior cycle. TSMC is the sole supplier of the A20 2nm chip with Apple modem replacing Qualcomm; Foxconn's allocation slips to 61% from 67% while Luxshare gains to 33% on Pro/Pro Max builds.

bullets.title: CIEN FY27 guided +30% to $8.4B+; supply-constrained through 2028, Hyper-Rail ramping to hundreds of millions
bullets.body: Ciena beat F3Q26 estimates and guided FY27 revenues to at least +30% y/y ($8.4B+) vs. consensus $8.0B, with gross margins of 45–46% and operating margins of 25–27%. Backlog is expected to exceed $10B at year-end FY26, with demand exceeding supply through 2027–2028. Hyper-Rail standardizes by end-2026 and ramps to several hundred million dollars in 2027 at above-average margins.

bullets.title: HPE -12% post-strong results; AI inferencing demand drives record backlog but supply constraints persist into 2027
bullets.body: HPE Q3 revenue of $12.21B beat by ~$240M with EPS $1.11 vs. $0.93 guidance; FY26 EPS raised to $3.75–$3.85 and FY27 guided +16–20%. Cloud & AI operating margin expanded to 17% from 7% y/y, and a $3.5B hyperscaler on-prem inference deal was announced. Despite the beat, the stock fell ~12% as supply constraints limiting networking upside persist into 2027 and some desks flag potential peak margins.

bullets.title: Nscale/Figure $3.5B–$6B NVIDIA Vera Rubin compute deal signals continued hyperscale GPU demand
bullets.body: Nscale signed a multi-year strategic partnership with humanoid robotics firm Figure involving an initial $3.5B compute commitment (scalable to $6B+) using NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform with up to 100,000 GPUs, targeted for deployment in Barstow, Texas starting H2 2027. The deal reinforces the sustained capital intensity of the AI infrastructure build-out.

bullets.title: DELL traditional server units down YoY; FY28 outlook flat-to-down units with ASP growth as key driver
bullets.body: Dell's traditional server units declined YoY despite the market falling 9% YoY, driven by supply shortages, SMB budget exhaustion, and enterprise consolidation to denser Gen 18 servers (5–7x replacement ratio). FY28 is expected to see flat-to-down units with ASP growth from richer configs and elevated memory pricing; AI servers will drive ISG growth but at lower margins than traditional server business.

bullets.title: LSE tokenization news drives SSNC +2.5%; institutional digital asset adoption accelerating
bullets.body: London Stock Exchange's plan to allow tokenized stocks on a 24-hour trading venue catalyzed a 2.5% intraday gain in SS&C, which UBS argues is well-positioned via its Calastone acquisition (~$1B, Jul-25) enabling tokenized fund distribution at scale. Bullish acquiring Equiniti (transfer agent serving 15k clients) for ~$4.2B (~4.6x sales) is cited as evidence of accelerating institutional digital asset adoption.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforming YTD +19% vs S&P 500 +13.4%; small-cap earnings tracking above revenue expectations
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 rose 1.1% on September 2, outperforming the S&P 500 by 0.7%, and is up 19.0% YTD vs. the S&P 500's 13.4%. With 84% of market cap reported for 2Q26, aggregate Russell 2000 revenues are running 3.3% above expectations while earnings are 0.1% below (5.1% beat ex-financials), suggesting healthy top-line momentum in small caps.
